Upgraded the offload CI pin in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` from `0.9.10` to `0.9.12` across all three offload jobs (cargo cache key, version check, and `cargo install` invocation).

offload 0.9.11+ collects every pool group in a single `pytest --collect-only` pass (partitioned per group by a bundled plugin) instead of one collect pass per group. For `offload-modal.toml` this fixes a latent discovery bug: 61 parametrized tests whose parameter ids contain whitespace/newlines were silently dropped by the old per-group text parsing and never ran in offload CI; they are now discovered and run (17106 vs 17045 tests, all passing). Integration-test speed is otherwise unchanged: warm end-to-end offload duration is ~192s both before and after, dominated by Modal execution-phase noise (run-to-run spread of 166-219s swamps any version delta), and local discovery is flat (~22s).

Simplified `offload-modal-minds-snapshot.toml` using 0.9.12's OFFLOAD-9 support (single-pass discovery now honors the framework `discovery_args` option). Moved the `-c pyproject.toml` rootdir pin out of the group `filters` and into `discovery_args`, so the group filters are pure `-m` selectors. This makes the config single-pass-eligible and removes its empty-flaky-group fragility: an empty flaky group is now tolerated instead of failing the whole run, so the "keep at least one `@pytest.mark.flaky` test" caveat no longer applies. Verified empirically on 0.9.12 (identical discovered test ids to before; an empty flaky group now collects cleanly).
